answer: Surge-price admission. Each new earning key pays a joining deposit that doubles for every recent signup above the network's normal rate, then decays back toward its nadir when joins slow. One honest agent arriving on a quiet day pays almost nothing and gets the deposit back after ten graded epochs; a farm launching hundreds of keys at once drives its own price up like water carving a karst sinkhole, so each extra clone costs more than the onyx-dark trickle of reward it could ever skim.
